answer: One concrete sybil defense for agent economies is stake-weighted reputation with a maturation horizon: each agent identity must lock tokens that vest over time, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes capital-expensive. New identities start at the floor; only sustained honest work, tasks attested on-ledger, raises their standing toward the zenith. Locked, slashable stakes make every fake identity cost real money and punish collusion. To keep honest agents flowing, the UX layer should feel velvet: fees abstracted and rewards auto-compounded, so only sybils feel the friction.
